item.research_question: How can high-entropy alloys be recommended effectively when existing data is limited, biased, and lacks sufficient descriptors for alloys with varying numbers of components?
item.material_system: Equiatomic alloys comprising elements from the set {Fe, Co, Ir, Cu, Ni, Pt, Pd, Rh, Au, Ag, Ru, Os, Si, As, Al, Tc, Re, Mn, Ta, Ti, W, Mo, Cr, V, Hf, Nb, Zr}, specifically focusing on Fe-Co-based quaternary alloys (FeMnCoNi) and early transition metal alloys.
item.processing_route: Development of an evidence-based recommender system (ERS) using Dempster–Shafer theory to model, collect, and combine pieces of evidence from existing datasets without using material descriptors; experimental validation involved synthesizing Fe0.25Co0.25Mn0.25Ni0.25 thin films annealed at 400 °C.
item.test_conditions: Evaluation performed via k-fold cross-validation on four datasets (ASMI16, CALPHAD, AFLOW, LTVC) containing binary, ternary, quaternary, and quinary alloys; extrapolation tests conducted on quaternary and quinary HEAs; experimental validation on thin films annealed at 400 °C.
key_findings: The ERS outperforms matrix-factorization (NMF, SVD) and supervised-learning (SVM, logistic regression, decision tree, naive Bayes) systems in k-fold cross-validation across all four datasets.
The ERS demonstrates superior extrapolation capabilities, requiring approximately 10–100 fewer trials to recall 50% and 75% of quinary HEAs compared to NMF and SVD systems.
Supervised-learning methods failed to rank HEAs effectively in datasets containing only positively labeled HEAs, performing either randomly or failing to rank any.
The ERS identified FeCoMnNi as the only Fe-Mn-Co-based quaternary candidate with a belief higher than 0.5.
Experimental validation confirmed that the Fe0.25Co0.25Mn0.25Ni0.25 thin film annealed at 400 °C exhibits a body-centered cubic (BCC) structure, evidenced by a reflection at 2θ = 44.7°.
Similarity analysis revealed three distinct element groups corresponding to early transition metals, late transition metals, and a third group with no evidence of similarity in the ASMI16 dataset.
Elements with the same periodic table group index (Δgroup = 0) showed high similarity scores, while similarity decreased as Δgroup increased to 3 or 4.
In the absence of sufficient evidence for mixtures of many elements, the system retained a large degree of uncertainty, with m({HEA, ¬HEA}) ≈ 1.
item.mechanism: The ERS uses the elemental substitution method where pairs of observed alloys serve as evidence to measure substitutability between element combinations; Dempster–Shafer theory assigns mass functions to subsets of a frame of discernment ({similar, dissimilar} or {HEA, ¬HEA}) to model uncertainty, combining multiple pieces of evidence using the Dempster rule to rank potential alloys without relying on material descriptors.
item.limitations: The system does not answer essential questions regarding the specific crystal structure or other properties of the HEAs beyond phase existence; detailed quantitative investigation of secondary phases in the synthesized FeCoMnNi alloy thin film was not done due to technical difficulties; the system cannot reliably recall the remaining one-quarter of HEAs in some datasets due to insufficient evidence in the training data.
item.future_work: The authors propose that by redesigning the frame of discernment to reflect additional properties of interest, the model can be constructed to recommend potential alloys forming HEA phases with desirable properties beyond just phase existence.
quotes: To overcome these issues, here we show the development of an evidence-based material recommender system (ERS) that adopts Dempster–Shafer theory, a general framework for reasoning with uncertainty.
We experimentally validated the most strongly recommended Fe–Co-based magnetic HEA (namely, FeCoMnNi) and confirmed that its thin film shows a body-centered cubic structure.

item.research_question: How can a recommender system be constructed to identify unknown High-Entropy Alloy (HEA) compositions and extrapolate recommendations to higher-order alloys (quaternary and quinary) based on binary and ternary training data?
item.material_system: Alloys composed of 27 elements; specific datasets include D_AFLOW (binary/ternary), D_LTVC (binary/ternary), D_ASMI16 (binary), D_CALPHAD (ternary); case study: Fe0.25Co0.25Mn0.25Ni0.25 thin films
item.processing_route: Machine learning: Grid search for hyperparameter α (0.01 to 0.9); Ninefold cross-validation repeated 100 times; Experimental: Combinatorial multitarget radio frequency sputtering (100 W FeCoMn, 120 W Ni) at 0.3 Pa Ar, deposition rate 0.23 ± 0.01 nm s–1, annealing at 400 °C for 30 min under vacuum < 6 × 10−3 Pa
item.test_conditions: Cross-validation on D_AFLOW (80% accuracy), D_LTVC (75% accuracy), D_ASMI16 (40/45 training, 5/45 test), D_CALPHAD (216/243 training, 27/243 test); Extrapolation to 17,550 quaternary and 80,730 quinary alloys; Thin film characterization via XRD and XRF
key_findings: Cross-validated testing accuracy rates were 80% for D_AFLOW and 75% for D_LTVC.
The absolute value of alpha (α) has little effect on the final result of the recommender system.
A total of 351 hypothetical binary alloys were generated from 27 elements, with 45 in the training set and 306 ranked by the model.
For ternary alloys, 2,925 hypothetical combinations were generated from 27 elements, with 243 in the training set and 2,682 ranked.
The model ranked 17,550 quaternary alloys and 80,730 quinary alloys for synthesis candidates.
The BCC phase was confirmed for the annealed thin film sample at the equiatomic composition of FeCoMnNi.
Phase separation and inflection points were observed near 400 °C for FeCoMn-X compositions.
item.mechanism: The system uses a rating matrix representation where alloys are decomposed into elementary components (A and B) to build a user-item matrix. It learns a similarity matrix between elements (and binary combinations) from training data to predict ratings for missing elements, allowing the ranking of hypothetical alloys. The method accounts for uncertainty by adding a degree of uncertainty α in the mass function.
item.limitations: The compositional descriptor cannot be applied in the case of having extrapolation in the number of components. The experiments do not use the selected alloys (test set) to improve the accuracy of the model for the next trial due to computational cost.
item.future_work: Structural changes at higher temperatures for FeCoMnNi are expected and are currently under investigation.
quotes: The compositional descriptor therefore cannot be applied in the case of having extrapolation in the number of components.
The absolute value of alpha has little effect on the final result of the recommender system.
The BCC phase was confirmed for the annealed thin film sample at the equiatomical composition of FeCoMnNi (x = 0.25).
